topic: SQL and AI using chatgpt, sql

market_analysis.why_now: Millions of data professionals and analysts are actively experimenting with ChatGPT to accelerate their SQL workflows, but most are writing vague prompts and getting mediocre results. The intersection of generative AI and SQL is the single fastest-growing skill search term on LinkedIn and YouTube in 2024-2025.
market_analysis.target_learner: Data analysts, junior developers, and business professionals who already know basic SQL SELECT statements but want to use ChatGPT to write, debug, and optimize queries 5x faster than doing it manually.
market_analysis.learner_goal: Use a proven prompt framework to get ChatGPT to generate accurate, production-ready SQL queries on the first try instead of going back and forth with vague prompts.
market_analysis.competition_gap: Most existing videos either show trivially simple examples like SELECT * FROM users or spend 20 minutes on setup. None give a repeatable prompt template the viewer can copy and use immediately with their own database schema. This video delivers a concrete framework in under 5 minutes.
market_analysis.platform_fit: YouTube Shorts and LinkedIn feed are ideal because the target audience — data professionals scrolling during work breaks — responds strongly to quick productivity hacks they can apply within minutes of watching.

content_structure.hook: Stop asking ChatGPT to write your SQL like this — you are giving it zero context and wondering why the queries are wrong. Here is the 3-line prompt framework that gets production-ready SQL on the first try.
content_structure.core_promise: You will learn a copy-paste prompt template that turns ChatGPT into a SQL expert that understands your exact database schema.

lessons.title: The 3-Line Prompt Framework for Perfect SQL from ChatGPT
lessons.learning_objective: By the end of this lesson the learner will be able to write a structured 3-part prompt — schema context, business question, and output constraints — that makes ChatGPT generate accurate, runnable SQL queries for any database.

scenes.scene_title: The Bad Prompt vs Good Prompt
scenes.what_learner_sees: Split screen showing ChatGPT. Left side: a vague prompt like 'write me a SQL query to get top customers' producing a generic, wrong query. Right side: the same request using the 3-line framework producing a perfect query with correct table and column names.
scenes.what_learner_hears: This is what most people type into ChatGPT — and this is the garbage they get back. The difference is not ChatGPT being dumb. The difference is you are not giving it the three things it needs. Let me show you the framework.
scenes.transition_to_next: So here are the three lines you need every single time.

scenes.what_learner_sees: ChatGPT prompt window with a clearly formatted prompt being typed in real time. Line 1: paste of a CREATE TABLE schema for orders, customers, and products tables. Line 2: a plain-English business question. Line 3: constraints like dialect, formatting, and no subqueries. The resulting SQL output appears below.
scenes.what_learner_hears: Line one: paste your schema. Do not describe your tables in English — give ChatGPT the actual CREATE TABLE statements. Line two: state the business question in plain language. Line three: add your constraints — what SQL dialect, any formatting rules, performance preferences. Watch what happens when we hit enter.
scenes.transition_to_next: Now let me prove this works on a real query you would actually run at work.

scenes.scene_title: Live Demo — Revenue by Customer Segment
scenes.what_learner_sees: The SQL query generated by ChatGPT is pasted into a SQL viewer connected to a sample database. The query runs successfully and returns a results table showing revenue by customer segment with correct joins across three tables. The schema panel on the left confirms the table structures match.
scenes.what_learner_hears: I am taking the exact SQL that ChatGPT just wrote and running it against our sample database. No edits. Look — it nailed the JOIN conditions, used the right column names, and even aliased everything cleanly. This is because we gave it the schema, not a vague description.
scenes.transition_to_next: But what about when you need to debug or optimize? Same framework, one extra line.

scenes.scene_title: Bonus — Debug and Optimize with One Extra Line
scenes.what_learner_sees: ChatGPT window showing the same prompt framework but with an intentionally broken query pasted in and a fourth line asking ChatGPT to identify the error and suggest a more performant alternative. ChatGPT responds with the fix and an optimized version using an index-friendly WHERE clause.
scenes.what_learner_hears: Got a query that is throwing errors or running slow? Add a fourth line: paste the broken query and ask ChatGPT to fix it and explain why. Same schema context, same constraints. It works because ChatGPT already understands your data model.

scenes.what_learner_sees: Clean slide showing the 3-line framework summarized: 1. Schema (CREATE TABLE statements), 2. Business Question (plain English), 3. Constraints (dialect, format, rules). A text overlay says 'Grab the prompt template — link in description.'
scenes.what_learner_hears: Schema, question, constraints. That is the framework. I left the prompt template and a sample database in the description so you can practice this in the next five minutes. If this saved you time, share it with your team.

lessons.key_takeaway: Always give ChatGPT your actual CREATE TABLE schema, a clear business question, and explicit constraints — this 3-line framework gets accurate SQL on the first prompt every time.

exercise_file_plan.purpose: A ready-to-use prompt template with placeholders for schema, business question, and constraints that the learner can copy-paste into ChatGPT and customize for their own database.
A SQLite database with orders, customers, and products tables pre-loaded with realistic sample data so the learner can run the generated SQL queries locally and verify results.
The CREATE TABLE statements for all three tables in the sample database, formatted and ready to paste into the prompt template as the schema context line.
